packageRules.description: Never update this repo's own image. docker-compose.yml must keep tracking the latest tag.
Automerge base image updates. pinDigest is the first pin, digest is every bump after.

description: Never automerge a GitHub Actions update. Human review is the only control that works here, so do not replace this rule with a delay such as minimumReleaseAge.

Why review is the only control: an action runs third-party code inside this workflow, where it can read DOCKERHUB_TOKEN and a GITHUB_TOKEN that holds contents:write and packages:write. That is enough to push a poisoned image to Docker Hub and GHCR and to create a release tag. A digest pin stops a moved tag from changing what runs, but it does not stop Renovate from raising a pull request that moves the pin to the attacker's commit. Only a person reading the diff catches that.

Why minimumReleaseAge does not help: for actions Renovate uses the github-tags datasource, which reports when a version was first released, not when its tag was last re-pushed. A tag force-pushed onto old code keeps the old timestamp and clears any delay at once.

This rule is deliberately blanket, with no matchUpdateTypes. Digest pinning changes the update type Renovate reports: a pinned SHA whose comment names an exact version, such as # v7.0.1, produces patch and minor updates, so a per-updateType automerge rule elsewhere in this file would silently switch automerge back on for action code. Keep the trailing comments at the major tag, for example # v7, and keep this rule last so it wins over any rule above it.
This does not affect the Dockerfile base image, which is matched by manager and still automerges.
